To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a random walk algorithm can be made to be effective by changing its randomly determined next direction based on the agent's own directional moving experiences.

a simple random walk can be improved by introducing a simple rule that controls its moving directions, and this simple rule can lead to an effective food searching strategy in an unknown and complex environment.

a simple random walk can be transformed into an effective search strategy, which exhibits super-diffusion and power-law-distribution properties, if an agent alters the direction of its randomly determined next move based on its own moving experiences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of a Lévy-like algorithm from a simple random-walk algorithm.
the emergence of a flexible search strategy from a random walk and the underlying dynamics that govern the search strategy.
the emergence of an effective foraging behavior, and we showed that a random walk algorithm that is based on a self-organizing mechanism can be an effective foraging strategy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a simple algorithm with a simple rule, which can be implemented in a real animal, can achieve an efficient search strategy in an environment with unknown food distributions.
our algorithm is more effective in finding a food source than a simple random walk, and the emergence of Lévy-like properties is a natural consequence of our algorithm.
the algorithm presented in this study represents an optimal search strategy, which can be achieved from a simple random-walk algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a simple random walk can be transformed into an optimal search strategy by introducing a simple rule based on its own moving experiences.
a simple random walk with a fixed move distance can be improved by a flexible exploration strategy, which can be realized through the agent’s own directional movement experiences.

a simple random walk with a simple rule for controlling the direction of the next move leads to a super-diffusive and effective food search strategy, and the power-law distribution is not a necessary condition for an effective search strategy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple algorithm can lead to an effective foraging performance, even if the agent has only limited information about its environment and its own movement.
an agent can achieve a flexible exploration strategy without any prior information of the environment by using a simple rule that controls its own random movement.
a simple rule for the random walk algorithm, based on the agent’s own experiences, is sufficient to generate an effective foraging performance.
